title: Compactly supported direct image of the open-closed triangle of a Weil complex
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ a prime; take $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ (Lean `PadicAlgCl ℓ`). Use the native category $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W)$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], the full subcategory of the derived category of pro-etale sheaves with an invertible Frobenius action consisting of the bounded objects with constructible cohomology (Lean `WeilComplex k₀ ℓ W`). Let $j:U\to X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion and $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion of $k_0$-schemes with complementary images. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated quasi-compact locally finite-type morphism over $k_0$, with $Y$ quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite type over $k_0$. For $K\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$ there is a distinguished triangle $T$ in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(Y)$ with isomorphisms
$$T_1\cong R(fj)_{0!}j^*K,\qquad T_2\cong Rf_{0!}K,\qquad T_3\cong R(fi)_{0!}i^*K.$$
Here all pullbacks and compactly supported direct images are the native equivariant derived constructions of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. The conclusion prescribes the vertices only, exactly as the recorded Lean declaration does.

proof.text: The structure map of $Y$ is finite type (locally finite type and quasi-compact). By finite-type composition, $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is finite type. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field, and its spectrum has one point, so $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is a Noetherian scheme. Finite type over a Noetherian scheme makes $X$ Noetherian. In particular it is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian; the cited quasi-separatedness lemma makes $X$ quasi-separated. Thus $X$ has all three absolute hypotheses needed for the native open-closed and composition statements. No absolute separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ is inferred.

source.place: clause 3: check the hypotheses on X for the open-closed triangle and composition

proof.text: The quasi-compact open immersion $j$ is finite type by the cited open-immersion lemma. It is separated: $U\to U\times_XU$ is an isomorphism because $j$ identifies $U$ with an open subscheme, so its diagonal is a closed immersion. The closed immersion $i$ is proper by the cited lemma, hence is separated and finite type. Applying finite-type composition to $j$ and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, and to $i$ and that structure map, gives locally finite-type source schemes $U,Z$ as required to use their native Weil categories. All maps are over $k_0$ by hypothesis. In particular both pairs $(j,f)$ and $(i,f)$ satisfy every hypothesis of native compact-support composition; $i$ satisfies those of proper coincidence with target $X$.

source.place: clause 3: the open and closed legs are separated finite type

proof.text: Apply the native open-closed triangle lemma to $(j,i,K)$, using step 1 for the absolute hypotheses on $X$. Choose its distinguished triangle $S$ and vertex isomorphisms $s_1:S_1\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{0!}j^*K$, $s_2:S_2\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, and $s_3:S_3\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_*i^*K$. All of these objects and isomorphisms belong to the native derived Weil category, so no passage from fixed pairs or choice of Frobenius action on a cone occurs.

source.place: clause 3: localization triangle before applying Rf!

proof.text: Put $F=Rf_{0!}$. The preservation and triangulation lemma applies to $f$ with exactly the stated hypotheses. Define $T=F(S)$: its first two arrows are $F$ of those of $S$, and its last arrow is $F(S_3)\to F(S_1[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(S_1)[1]$, using the derived shift comparison. The cited lemma says precisely that this is a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(Y)$, with vertices $T_r=F(S_r)$.

source.place: clause 3: applying Rf! to the localization triangle

proof.text:
Let $c_{j,f}:R(fj)_{0!}\xrightarrow{\sim}F\circ Rj_{0!}$ and $c_{i,f}:R(fi)_{0!}\xrightarrow{\sim}F\circ Ri_{0!}$ be the native composition isomorphisms. Let $p_i:Ri_{0!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_*$ be proper coincidence for the proper map $i$ (its target $X$ has the hypotheses checked in step 1). The following composites of isomorphisms identify the three vertices:
$$T_1=F(S_1)\xrightarrow{F(s_1)}F(Rj_{0!}j^*K)\xrightarrow{c_{j,f}^{-1}}R(fj)_{0!}j^*K,$$
$$T_2=F(S_2)\xrightarrow{F(s_2)}F(K),$$
$$T_3=F(S_3)\xrightarrow{F(s_3)}F(Ri_*i^*K)\xrightarrow{F(p_i^{-1})}F(Ri_{0!}i^*K)\xrightarrow{c_{i,f}^{-1}}R(fi)_{0!}i^*K.$$
Here each functor isomorphism is evaluated at the displayed object. A functor maps an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse morphisms, since it preserves composition and identities. Thus these are isomorphisms in the Weil category itself. Keeping $T$ from step 4 and these three vertex isomorphisms gives exactly the existential conclusion. There is no need to assert that any of the arrows is a preassigned counit, unit or boundary.

theorem exists_distTriang_derivedLowerShriek_openClosed (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [QuasiCompact j] [j.IsOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [i.IsOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (hij : IsCompl (Set.range j.base) (Set.range i.base))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (K : WeilComplex k₀ l X) :
    ∃ T ∈ distTriang (WeilComplex k₀ l Y),
      Nonempty (T.obj₁ ≅ (derivedLowerShriek k₀ l (j ≫ f)).obj ((upperStar j).obj K)) ∧
      Nonempty (T.obj₂ ≅ (derivedLowerShriek k₀ l f).obj K) ∧
      Nonempty (T.obj₃ ≅ (derivedLowerShriek k₀ l (i ≫ f)).obj ((upperStar i).obj K)) :=
  sorry
